consequence: CallActivity_77 (GLOVIA_Conditioncheck_Salesorder_Create.groovy) and CallActivity_86 (Content Modifier for OrganizationId) are defined in the BPMN model but have no connecting incoming/outgoing sequence flows. The validation logic for order types is never executed during runtime, potentially leading to incorrect router evaluation.
mitigation: Wire CallActivity_77 and CallActivity_86 sequentially between CallActivity_4 and ExclusiveGateway_80. Write unit tests validating that 'OrderCodeValid' and 'OrganizationId' headers are populated.

consequence: In CallActivity_4, the property 'InputPayload' is created using expression '${in.body}'. For high-volume or oversized payloads, caching large string payloads in Camel exchange properties causes JVM heap exhaustion.
mitigation: Enforce strict XML maximum body size thresholds (already configured to 40MB in SOAP adapter) and test boundary size limit behaviors.

consequence: EndEvent_11 raises an escalation event ('RoutingConditionNotMet'). If external sender Glovia expects standard SOAP acknowledgements, an unhandled escalation fault can cause retry storms from the sender system.
mitigation: Implement explicit test assertions for SOAP 1.1 Fault compliance and ensure receiver error contracts accept the escalation fault format.

consequence: The router conditions '{{Glovia_Route_SalesOrder}}' and '{{Glovia_Route2_ReturnSalesOrder}}' rely on tenant parameters. If unconfigured or misconfigured, all traffic diverts to default Escalation End.
mitigation: Create automated smoke tests validating parameter injection across deployment pipelines before activating endpoints.
